one_liner: Single-threaded C++ LRU cache library plus a memcached-text-protocol server that fits 7-16% more data than Memcached in the same RAM.
what_it_does: Two things share one codebase. libcachelot is an embeddable, fixed-size, in-process key-value LRU cache (C++ class cache::Cache plus a C API) that allocates its memory arena once at startup and can either evict or return an out-of-memory error when full. cachelotd is a standalone server that speaks the memcached ASCII protocol over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, so existing memcached text clients can connect to it on port 11211. It is not a full memcached replacement: the binary protocol handler just throws not_implemented, and some commands behave differently (see gotchas).
how_it_is_fast: The memory gain comes from the allocator, not the index. One power-of-two arena is split into fixed pages (1 MB by default). Inside each page, items are variable-size blocks with an 8-byte header, kept on segregated free lists (power-of-two ranges each cut into 32 sub-classes, TLSF-style), and split or coalesced with their neighbours. Each item is stored close to its exact size, instead of being rounded up to a slab-class chunk as in memcached. Items keep the key and value inline behind a compact header (64-bit CAS stamp, 32-bit hash, length, expiry, 16-bit flags). The index is a Robin Hood open-addressing hash table with hashes stored in a separate array, FNV-1a 32-bit hashing and a 93% max load factor, and it grows by incremental two-table rehashing to avoid resize stalls. There are no locks anywhere.
when_to_use: A memcached text-protocol cache that is memory-bound with mostly small values (10 B-1 KB): the vendor chart shows about 91-94% of a 2 GB budget holding live data vs about 79.5% for Memcached
Embedding a hard-capped LRU cache inside a single-threaded event loop, or one instance per core/shard, where you want no malloc after startup and predictable memory use
Resource-limited targets (the README lists 32-bit ARM and x86-64) where the cache must never exceed a fixed arena
'Consistent cache' use (-M / enable_evictions=false), where a full cache should return an error instead of silently evicting data
C or FFI embedding through the provided C API (cachelot_set/get/add/cas-style calls and an eviction callback)
when_not_to_use: You need one multi-threaded process or concurrent readers. The author states it is not thread-safe by design, and even get() mutates the LRU state, so you must shard or put it behind a single worker queue
You need full memcached compatibility: there is no binary protocol, no SASL/TLS, no meta commands and no 'stats <arg>'; flush_all and exptime semantics differ; flags are 16-bit

You pick a cache for throughput or latency. The only published comparison is memory efficiency; the 'faster latency' claim has no numbers, and siblings such as Pelikan, MemC3 and Pogocache publish throughput data
Hit ratio is sensitive to eviction precision. LRU is tracked per page (1 MB by default), and an eviction drops every item on the chosen page whatever their individual recency
You need a maintained, security-reviewed daemon. The last commit was April 2023, the only CI config is a legacy .travis.yml (no GitHub Actions), and several CLI flags are silently ignored

integration.form: static lib (libcachelot, mostly inline headers plus a few .cpp files) and a cachelotd server binary; Docker image cachelot/cachelot
integration.dependencies: Boost >= 1.53 (system, program_options and asio for the server, unit_test_framework for tests; the library itself uses Boost error_code/intrusive pieces); CMake
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11); GCC, Clang or MSVC (VS 2022 via vcpkg for Boost on Windows)
integration.platforms: x86-64 and 32-bit ARM; the README says it is tested on Alpine, CentOS 7, Ubuntu, macOS and Windows 10/11
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe by design (cache.h note; author in issues #24, #28, #35 and #40). Concurrent reads are unsafe too, because get() touches the page LRU and lookups can advance incremental rehashing. Stats counters are one process-global, non-atomic struct shared by all Cache instances.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the memcached ASCII protocol on port 11211 works for get/gets/set/add/replace/cas/append/prepend/delete/incr/decr/touch/stats/version/flush_all/quit, but the binary protocol is unimplemented and flush_all, exptime and flags semantics differ

gotchas: flush_all only removes items that have already expired; unlike memcached, it does not invalidate live items. exptime is always taken as relative seconds, with no absolute-Unix-time rule for values over 30 days, so absolute expiries effectively never fire

The server's -d (daemon), -l (listen), -C (no-cas) and socket-access flags are parsed but never applied (issue #15 confirms -d is unimplemented). TCP and UDP both bind to all interfaces on 11211 by default, and UDP memcached on a public interface is a known reflection-amplification vector, so pass -U 0 or firewall it

Eviction works per page: touching an item promotes its whole page, and evicting a page frees every item on it after a linear scan of the page table. A smaller -P page gives finer eviction but also caps the maximum item size, because an item must fit in one page
-m and -P must be powers of two. Library calls throw system_error (out_of_memory, key_too_long, item_too_big), and the pointer returned by do_get is valid only until the next Cachelot call
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Cachelot over Pelikan/Segcache, MemC3, Pogocache or Dragonfly only when RAM efficiency on a memcached-text workload, or an embeddable fixed-arena single-threaded LRU library, matters more than throughput; those siblings publish multi-threaded throughput wins over Memcached (for example Segcache at about 8x with 24 threads) and are better choices for a maintained, concurrent server.
verified_claims_summary: The author's own chart (cachelot.io, circa 2016) fills Cachelot and Memcached, each capped at 2 GB, with the same shuffled random dataset over 10 runs and counts surviving key+value bytes. Cachelot keeps 91-94% of the budget vs 79.5% for Memcached on 10 B-1 KB values, 94-99% vs 86.7% on 1-4 KB, 93-97% vs 87.3% on 4 KB-1 MB, and 93-97% vs 86.9% on mixed sizes, which is 7-16% more stored data by the 10th run. Cachelot's figures fall slightly each run while Memcached's stay flat. No CPU, compiler, flags or Memcached version is given, and the script in the repo now uses 4 GB, not 2 GB.
status_note: Abandoned since the last commit on 2023-04-12, but the BSD-2-Clause library is small and self-contained apart from Boost, so it is easy to vendor; treat the cachelotd daemon as unhardened.
